commitments.quote: It applies to all agreements under which Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits Protected Health Information for or on behalf of Covered Entity (the "Underlying Agreements").
commitments.summary: The BAA applies to every agreement under which Business Associate handles PHI for Covered Entity, which sets the reach of all the BAA duties.
commitments.scope: All agreements under which Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI for or on behalf of Covered Entity.
commitments.deviation: The BAA reaches all Underlying Agreements that involve PHI, while DPA 2.1 applies only to the Agreement the customer accepts and to Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.summary: Security Incident is limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors handle for Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: Incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.deviation: The BAA uses the HIPAA definition of Security Incident, which is not limited to confirmed events, while DPA 1.3 covers only confirmed Personal Data Breaches.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only for performing the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as the BAA permits.
commitments.scope: PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA permits uses needed to perform the Underlying Agreements, required by law, or allowed by the BAA, while DPA 2.2 limits processing to documented instructions.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: Uses and disclosures of PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA adds a minimum-necessary limit on uses and disclosures, which DPA 2.2 does not contain.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the result only to provide and improve the services.
commitments.scope: PHI that Business Associate de-identifies.
commitments.deviation: The BAA limits de-identification to the HIPAA safe harbor method and limits use of the result to providing and improving services, while DPA 8.2 allows Usage Data to be used to operate, secure and improve the Services.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Information de-identified under Section 2.3 falls outside PHI and outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Information de-identified in accordance with Section 2.3.
commitments.deviation: The BAA expressly removes de-identified information from the BAA, while DPA 1.6 only defines Usage Data as aggregated or de-identified data and does not exclude it from the DPA.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: A limited data set is treated as PHI for every purpose of the BAA.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e).
commitments.deviation: The BAA treats limited data sets as PHI, while DPA 1.1 defines Customer Personal Data without any limited-data-set category.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA incorporates the HIPAA Security Rule by reference, while DPA 4.1 relies on the security measures listed in Annex 2.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: PHI.
commitments.deviation: DPA 6.1 stores data in the customer's selected region and DPA 6.2 allows access from outside it, including Manila, under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism, while the BAA prohibits any storage, processing or access outside the United States with no transfer mechanism.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires HITRUST r2 certification for PHI systems, while DPA 4.2 requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 for the Services.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI to Covered Entity no later than ten calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach, a term defined in the HIPAA Rules that Section 1.1 incorporates

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Breach of Unsecured PHI, using the HIPAA definition of Breach.
commitments.deviation: The BAA sets a ten-calendar-day limit from HIPAA Discovery for a Breach of Unsecured PHI, while DPA 7.1 requires notice within 72 hours after the provider confirms a Personal Data Breach.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any Security Incident within five business days after it becomes aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becoming aware of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents as defined in Section 1.2, limited to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires reporting of any Security Incident within five business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it, while DPA 7.1 covers only confirmed Personal Data Breaches with notice within 72 hours after confirmation.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts are treated as noticed by Section 4.2 and need no further report.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA handles unsuccessful attempts by deeming them noticed and requiring no further report, while DPA 1.3 excludes them from the definition of Personal Data Breach.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA within ten calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becoming aware of the use or disclosure

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA, including non-permitted uses that are not Breaches.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: Reports under Section 4 must be made in writing to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example; copy to Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: All reports under Section 4.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires written reports to named Privacy Office and Information Security Office addresses, while DPA 7.2 sends notice to the security contact in the administration console or to the account owner.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, the affected individuals, the PHI involved, the Breach and Discovery dates, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires identification of each affected individual and the Breach and Discovery dates, while DPA 7.3 requires the nature of the breach, the data categories and the measures taken, and provides for later updates.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media for a Breach it or its Subcontractors caused.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must bind each Subcontractor that handles PHI for it, in writing, to the same restrictions that apply to Business Associate.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on Business Associate's behalf.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires a written flow-down of the same restrictions, while DPA 5.5 makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessor performance without requiring a written flow-down.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten business days after its request.
commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary for compliance review.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA gives government access to internal records for HIPAA compliance, while DPA 9.3 gives the customer a limited on-site audit right and treats reports as satisfying audit rights.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must return or destroy all PHI within thirty days after termination of the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: All PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires return or destruction of all PHI within 30 days after termination, while DPA 10.1 allows 90 days for deletion and a further 35 days for backups.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate must keep extending the BAA protections to the PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.scope: PHI that cannot feasibly be returned or destroyed.
commitments.deviation: The BAA extends BAA protections indefinitely while infeasible PHI is retained, while DPA 10.1 deals only with deletion timing and backup overwriting.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA overrides the Subscription Agreement and any Vendor or Affiliate data processing terms, policies or online terms.
commitments.deviation: Also overrides Vendor and Affiliate policies and online terms, which DPA 11.1 does not mention; DPA 11.1 only makes the DPA control over the Agreement.

commitments.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: Retailer Data covers all data Retailer, its employees or customers provide or Vendor collects from Retailer systems, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and derived data.
commitments.scope: All data provided by or collected from Retailer, its employees or customers, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and derived data; not limited to personal data.
commitments.deviation: Covers all Retailer data, not only personal data contained in Customer Data as DPA 1.1 defines Customer Personal Data; also covers telemetry, logs, traces and derived data.

commitments.quote: "Data Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.summary: A Data Incident is any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while a Subprocessor holds it.
commitments.scope: Actual or reasonably suspected incidents involving any Retailer Data, including data held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: DPA 1.3 covers only breaches ExampleCo has confirmed involving Customer Personal Data and excludes unsuccessful attempts; this covers suspected incidents involving all Retailer Data, including at Subprocessors.

commitments.quote: "Subprocessor" means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.summary: A Subprocessor is any third party or Vendor Affiliate that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.scope: Any third party or Vendor Affiliate processing Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.deviation: Expressly includes Vendor Affiliates and applies to Retailer Data rather than Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: Processing of Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Limits processing to the Services in the Subscription Agreement and to Retailer's written instructions; DPA 2.2 also allows instructions set in the Agreement, the DPA and customer configuration.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.scope: Any machine learning model; exception for models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.deviation: Broader than DPA 8.1, which bars training only foundation models made available to other customers; this bars any machine learning model, excepting only models used solely for Retailer.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Vendor may store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Storage of Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Fixes storage to the United States or Canada, whereas DPA 6.1 stores data in the hosting region the customer selects; the contract addresses storage only and says nothing about access from other locations, which DPA 6.2 covers.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.deviation: Sets the CIS Critical Security Controls IG2 benchmark instead of the Annex 2 measures, and has no DPA 4.1 allowance for updates that do not materially reduce security.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: Retailer Data at rest and in transit.
commitments.deviation: Requires only industry-standard encryption without naming a cipher or TLS version, whereas Annex 2 specifies AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year.
commitments.scope: The Services.
commitments.deviation: DPA 4.2 requires both a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification; this contract requires only an annual SOC 2 Type II report.

commitments.quote: provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request
commitments.summary: Vendor must provide the SOC 2 Type II report to Retailer within 15 days after Retailer's request.
commitments.scope: The SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.deviation: DPA 9.1 makes the report available through the Trust Center subject to acceptance of non-disclosure terms; this contract requires delivery to Retailer within 15 days of a request and states no non-disclosure condition.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not let any Subprocessor not listed in Appendix B process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Subprocessors not listed in Appendix B.
commitments.deviation: Requires Retailer's prior written consent for new Subprocessors instead of DPA 5.1's general authorization with a Trust Center list.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data.
commitments.summary: Vendor must request Retailer's written consent for a new Subprocessor at least 30 days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data.

deadline.anchor: the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.scope: New Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: Requires a written consent request rather than notice by Trust Center update and email to subscribed customers.

commitments.quote: Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: Retailer's silence does not count as consent to a new Subprocessor.
commitments.scope: New Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: DPA 5.2 has no statement that silence is not consent; DPA 5.1 instead gives general authorization to engage Subprocessors.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA
commitments.summary: Vendor must bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as the VDPA.
commitments.scope: Each Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: Adds a written flow-down requirement that DPA 5.5 does not contain; DPA 5.5 covers only ExampleCo's responsibility for Subprocessor performance.

commitments.quote: remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.scope: Each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.deviation: Refers to acts and omissions generally, whereas DPA 5.5 refers only to Subprocessors' performance of the DPA obligations.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor becomes aware of the Data Incident

commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and +1 (614) 555-0182 (Section 6.2)
commitments.scope: Data Incidents as defined in Section 2.3, including reasonably suspected incidents and incidents at Subprocessors; the clock runs from Vendor's awareness, not confirmation.
commitments.deviation: Sets 24 hours from Vendor's awareness of any Data Incident, including suspected ones, instead of DPA 7.1's 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182.
commitments.summary: Vendor must send Data Incident notice by email to Retailer Security Operations and by telephone to the listed number.
commitments.scope: Data Incident notices.
commitments.deviation: Specifies email and telephone contacts for Retailer Security Operations, whereas DPA 7.2 sends notice to the security contact in the administration console or else the account owner.

commitments.quote: Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy the notice requirement in Section 6.1.
commitments.scope: Notice to account or procurement contacts.
commitments.deviation: Excludes account and procurement contacts as valid notice recipients; DPA 7.2 falls back to the account owner when no security contact is designated.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.summary: Vendor's notice must describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.scope: Data Incident notices.
commitments.deviation: Requires identifying any Subprocessor involved and does not include DPA 7.3's categories of data affected or its 'to the extent then known' qualifier.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: Vendor must supplement the Data Incident notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.scope: Data Incident notices.
commitments.deviation: Substantively similar to DPA 7.3, which says ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident without Retailer's prior written approval, unless required by law.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents involving Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation of a Data Incident.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.summary: Vendor must bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent Vendor or its Subprocessors caused it.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Sets 30 days, shorter than DPA 10.1's 90 days after termination, and has no DPA 10.1 backup overwrite period of a further 35 days.

commitments.quote: and confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.
commitments.summary: Vendor must confirm the deletion of Retailer Data to Retailer in writing within the same 30-day period.
commitments.scope: Deletion of Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Requires written confirmation without a customer request, whereas DPA 10.2 provides certification only upon the customer's written request.

commitments.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with the VDPA once per calendar year on 30 days' notice.
commitments.scope: Compliance with this VDPA.
commitments.deviation: DPA 9.3 allows one on-site audit per 12 months on 60 days' notice, during business hours and at customer expense, and only where a supervisory authority requires it; this allows an annual compliance audit on 30 days' notice with no stated business-hours or cost terms.

commitments.quote: within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance within 10 days after notice following a Data Incident.
commitments.scope: Compliance with this VDPA following a Data Incident.
commitments.deviation: Adds an audit right after a Data Incident on a 10-day timeline; DPA 9.3 provides for an additional audit only where a supervisory authority requires one.

commitments.quote: This VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.summary: The VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: A change of control of Vendor, by merger, acquisition or otherwise, does not terminate or modify this VDPA.
commitments.summary: A change of control of Vendor does not terminate or modify the VDPA.
commitments.scope: Change of control of Vendor by merger, acquisition or otherwise.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.summary: An acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.scope: Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Hosting | United States
commitments.summary: Amazon Web Services, Inc. is an approved Subprocessor for hosting, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: Hosting of Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: DPA 5.1 relies on a Trust Center list with general authorization; this contract approves named Subprocessors in an appendix.

commitments.quote: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | United States
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. is an approved Subprocessor for support ticketing, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: Support ticketing involving Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: DPA 5.1 relies on a Trust Center list with general authorization; this contract approves named Subprocessors in an appendix.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
commitments.summary: Amendment No. 1 adds ExampleCo, Inc., a Vendor Affiliate, as an approved Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features for the Services, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: Platform hosting and AI features for the Services.
commitments.deviation: Adds a Vendor Affiliate as an approved Subprocessor for AI features by appendix amendment dated September 8, 2025; DPA 8.3 instead lists AI model providers as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: The Addendum prevails over conflicting terms in the Agreement, order forms, data processing addenda, privacy policies and other Supplier documents.
commitments.deviation: Contract makes this Addendum control over the Agreement, order forms and any DPA, whereas the baseline says only the DPA controls over the Agreement as to processing of Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms incorporated by reference from Supplier websites, including trust or security sites, do not bind Bank or modify the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Terms incorporated by reference to Supplier websites, including trust or security sites.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Bank Data covers all data in any form that Supplier or a Subcontractor handles under the Agreement, including metadata, logs and derived or de-identified data.
commitments.scope: Includes data from Bank or its customers, metadata, logs and configuration data, and derived data such as model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized data.
commitments.deviation: Broader than Customer Personal Data: covers all data in any form, not only personal data, and includes metadata, logs and de-identified or derived data.

commitments.quote: means the earliest time at which Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of a Security Incident.
commitments.summary: Discovery is the earliest time Supplier or a Subcontractor knew or, with reasonable diligence, would have known of a Security Incident, and it starts the notice clocks.
commitments.deviation: Clock starts at constructive knowledge by Supplier or any Subcontractor, whereas the baseline trigger is ExampleCo's confirmation of a Personal Data Breach.

commitments.quote: any actual or reasonably suspected (a) unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of, Bank Data; or (b) unauthorized access to any system of Supplier or any Subcontractor that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data, whether or not unauthorized access to Bank Data has been confirmed.
commitments.summary: A Security Incident is any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or use of Bank Data, or unauthorized access to a Supplier or Subcontractor system holding Bank Data, whether or not Bank Data access is confirmed.
commitments.scope: Covers suspected incidents and unauthorized access to systems holding Bank Data, even without confirmed access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: Broader than the baseline: includes reasonably suspected incidents, non-personal Bank Data, and system-level access without confirmed data access; contains no exclusion for unsuccessful attempts.

commitments.quote: any third party, including any Supplier Affiliate, that Supplier engages to perform any part of the Services or that has access to Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Subcontractor means any third party, including a Supplier Affiliate, that performs any part of the Services or has access to Bank Data.
commitments.scope: Includes Supplier Affiliates and any third party with access to Bank Data, not only third parties that process it.
commitments.deviation: Broader than Subprocessor: includes Supplier Affiliates and any third party with access to Bank Data, not only third parties that process it.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a written information security program consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook.
commitments.deviation: Requires a written program aligned to the NIST CSF and FFIEC handbook, whereas the baseline requires implementing the Annex 2 measures, which ExampleCo may update.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Supplier must encrypt Bank Data at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: Adds 'or stronger' at rest and applies to all Bank Data, whereas baseline Annex 2 specifies AES-256 at rest for Customer Data; TLS 1.2 matches.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems holding Bank Data.
commitments.scope: Remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline requires MFA for access to production systems; contract requires it for all remote access to systems holding Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must complete criminal background checks on Supplier Personnel before they access Bank Data, where the law permits.
commitments.scope: All Supplier Personnel, including those of Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: Baseline requires only written confidentiality obligations; contract adds criminal background checks before access, to the extent permitted by law.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services throughout the term.
commitments.scope: The Services.
commitments.deviation: Requires a current SOC 2 Type II report for the full term but does not include the ISO/IEC 27001 certification the baseline also requires.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: Supplier must store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.scope: Storage and processing of all Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: Requires US-only storage and processing of all Bank Data; the baseline stores Customer Personal Data in the customer-selected hosting region and does not restrict processing location.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not allow Supplier Personnel outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel located outside the United States, including for support or maintenance.
commitments.deviation: Prohibits offshore access, including for support, absent Bank's prior written approval; the baseline permits access from outside the hosting region, including from Manila, under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 may access Bank Data, and each only within its listed scope.
commitments.scope: Access to Bank Data by Subcontractors, limited to the scope stated for each in Schedule 2.
commitments.deviation: No general authorization: access is limited to named Schedule 2 Subcontractors within their stated scope, whereas the baseline grants general authorization with a list published on the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least 90 days' prior written notice before adding or replacing a Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.

deadline.anchor: adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office, tprm-notices@anb.example, with a copy to Awesome National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001
commitments.scope: Adding or replacing any Subcontractor and expanding any Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.deviation: Notice period is 90 days instead of 30, delivered to a named Bank office under Exhibit C with a legal copy; the baseline gives notice by updating the Trust Center and emailing subscribers.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days after receiving notice of a new or expanded Subcontractor, and an objection stops engagement for Bank or lets Bank terminate without penalty with a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the notice under Section 5.2

commitments.scope: Objections to new or replaced Subcontractors and expanded Approved Subcontractor scopes.
commitments.deviation: Objection window is 30 days instead of 15, with no stated grounds requirement; an objection bars engagement or allows termination without penalty and with a pro-rata refund, rather than termination as the sole remedy.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Each Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.scope: Any Security Incident affecting a Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier is fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.scope: Acts and omissions of all Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: Makes Supplier fully liable for Subcontractor acts and omissions, whereas the baseline makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.

commitments.scope: Any Security Incident, including suspected incidents and incidents at Subcontractors.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give incident notice by telephone and email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center.
commitments.recipient: Bank's Cyber Fusion Center: telephone +1 (212) 555-0147 (24x7) and email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example
commitments.scope: Notices under Section 6.1.
commitments.deviation: Requires telephone and email to a named Bank security center; the baseline sends notice by email to the designated security contact or account owner.

commitments.quote: Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Notice only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy the incident notice requirement.
commitments.scope: Notice channels that do not count under Section 6.1.
commitments.deviation: Expressly excludes relationship-manager, status page and trust site notice; the baseline routes notice to the console security contact or account owner.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: Supplier's initial notice must include all information then known, including the Discovery time, systems and Subcontractors involved, and categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.scope: Initial notice of any Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: Requires specific content, including Discovery time, systems and Subcontractors, and categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected; the baseline covers nature, data categories and measures, to the extent then known.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must provide written status updates at least every 24 hours until the Security Incident is contained.
commitments.scope: Any Security Incident until containment.
commitments.deviation: Adds written status updates every 24 hours until containment; the baseline only commits to provide further information as it becomes available.

commitments.quote: shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment of a Security Incident.
commitments.scope: Any Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: Requires a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment; the baseline has no root-cause report.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law. Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not notify Bank's customers, regulators, law enforcement or the media about a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's written consent unless law requires it, and must tell Bank first where law requires it.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment
commitments.summary: Supplier must preserve logs, images and forensic evidence for a Security Incident for at least one year after containment.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.

commitments.scope: Forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.scope: Obligations owed to ANB Securities LLC.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.scope: Any notice period in the Addendum, Agreement, exhibits, schedules or applicable law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any AI or machine learning model, except a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data and any AI or machine learning model.
commitments.deviation: Broader than the baseline: bars use of Bank Data to evaluate or improve any AI or machine learning model, not only training foundation models available to other customers.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not allow anyone to review, label or annotate Bank Data to develop or improve a model, except an Approved Subcontractor expressly permitted in Schedule 2.
commitments.scope: Review, labeling or annotation of Bank Data for developing or improving any model.

commitments.summary: Supplier must list in Schedule 2 every third-party model provider that receives Bank Data.

commitments.summary: Supplier must ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.

commitments.deviation: Requires Supplier to ensure no retention after a response, with no abuse-monitoring exception; the baseline requires providers not to retain beyond response time except for abuse monitoring.

commitments.summary: Supplier must have an independent third party penetration test the Services at least once every 12 months.

commitments.scope: The Services.

commitments.quote: and shall deliver an executive summary of the results to Bank within thirty (30) days after Bank's request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver an executive summary of penetration test results to Bank within 30 days after Bank's request.
commitments.scope: Results of penetration tests of the Services.
commitments.deviation: Executive summary goes to Bank within 30 days of Bank's request, instead of being made available through the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall remediate vulnerabilities rated Critical within fifteen (15) days, and vulnerabilities rated High within thirty (30) days, after identification.
commitments.summary: Supplier must remediate Critical vulnerabilities within 15 days after identification.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall remediate vulnerabilities rated Critical within fifteen (15) days, and vulnerabilities rated High within thirty (30) days, after identification.
commitments.summary: Supplier must remediate High vulnerabilities within 30 days after identification.
commitments.scope: Vulnerabilities rated High.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.summary: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance once in any 12-month period on 30 days' written notice.

commitments.quote: and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice.

commitments.scope: Audits after any Security Incident.

commitments.quote: Nothing in this Addendum limits the access of any regulator with authority over Bank.
commitments.summary: Nothing in the Addendum limits access by any regulator with authority over Bank.
commitments.scope: Access by any regulator with authority over Bank.
commitments.deviation: Preserves regulator access without the Addendum's audit limits; the baseline limits further audits to one on-site audit per 12 months.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services with a recovery time objective of no more than four (4) hours and a recovery point objective of no more than one (1) hour.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services with a 4-hour recovery time objective and a 1-hour recovery point objective.
commitments.scope: The Services.

deadline.anchor: the previous plan test (inferred; no anchor stated)

commitments.scope: The business continuity and disaster recovery plan.
commitments.deviation: Baseline requires annual testing; contract adds delivery of the test results summary to Bank.

commitments.quote: participate in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on sixty (60) days' written notice.
commitments.summary: Supplier must participate in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on 60 days' written notice.
commitments.scope: Bank's annual operational resilience exercise.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain cyber liability insurance with limits of no less than twenty-five million dollars ($25,000,000) per claim throughout the term of the Agreement and for two (2) years after.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain cyber liability insurance of at least $25,000,000 per claim throughout the term and for two years after.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.summary: Supplier must return Bank Data to Bank in the format Bank reasonably requests within 30 days after termination or Bank's written request.

commitments.quote: then securely destroy all Bank Data, including in backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: After returning Bank Data, Supplier must securely destroy all Bank Data, including backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request

commitments.quote: Within ten (10) business days after destruction, Supplier shall deliver a certificate of destruction signed by an officer of Supplier.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver an officer-signed certificate of destruction within 10 business days after destruction.

commitments.summary: Exhibit D applies to Supplier's processing of customer information of ANB Securities LLC, a registered broker-dealer.

commitments.quote: a breach of security of the Services that ExampleCo has confirmed led to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, Customer Personal Data.

commitments.scope: Breaches of the security of the Services affecting Customer Personal Data, once ExampleCo has confirmed them.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.scope: Usage Data as defined in Section 1.6.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo lists the third-party model providers used by AI features as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo lists the third-party model providers used by its AI features as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Third-party model providers used by AI features.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except for abuse monitoring.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs processed by AI model providers; abuse monitoring is excepted.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will make its most recent SOC 2 Type II report available to Customer through the Trust Center, subject to Customer's acceptance of the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo will make its most recent SOC 2 Type II report available to Customer through the Trust Center, subject to acceptance of its non-disclosure terms.
commitments.scope: ExampleCo's most recent SOC 2 Type II report.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually.
commitments.scope: Penetration test of the Services.

commitments.quote: will make an executive summary of the results available through the Trust Center
commitments.summary: ExampleCo will make an executive summary of penetration test results available through the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Executive summary of penetration test results.

commitments.quote: Customer agrees that the reports in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws.
commitments.summary: Customer agrees that the SOC 2 report and penetration test summary satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws.
commitments.scope: Reports in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 as audit substitutes under Data Protection Laws.

commitments.quote: Where a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve (12) month period
commitments.summary: Where a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve-month period.
commitments.scope: Only where a supervisory authority requires a further audit.

commitments.quote: with at least sixty (60) days' written notice, during business hours, and at Customer's expense.
commitments.summary: Customer must give at least 60 days' written notice of an on-site audit, which must take place during business hours at Customer's expense.
commitments.scope: On-site audits conducted under Section 9.3.

commitments.quote: Within ninety (90) days after termination or expiry of the Agreement, ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services within 90 days after termination or expiry of the Agreement.

deadline.anchor: termination or expiry of the Agreement

commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data in the Services.

commitments.quote: Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further thirty-five (35) days.
commitments.summary: Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further 35 days after the 90-day deletion period.

deadline.anchor: end of the 90-day deletion period in Section 10.1

commitments.scope: Backups containing Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion upon Customer's written request.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion when the customer requests it in writing.
commitments.scope: Deletion of Customer Personal Data under Section 10.

commitments.quote: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls as to the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.summary: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls for the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.scope: Processing of Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: Customer Data; the DPA does not define this term.

commitments.quote: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.summary: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.scope: Access to production systems.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.
commitments.scope: The Services.

commitments.quote: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws are made under the Standard Contractual Clauses, Module 2 or Module 3 as applicable.
commitments.summary: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws are made under the Standard Contractual Clauses, Module 2 or Module 3 as applicable.
commitments.scope: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws.
